reproduction.rationale: Task identity binds the explicitly released future canonical preimage; atomic binder adoption must produce exactly those bytes. Reproduction is a valid independent goal, but both matched information conditions lack immutable complete original-data/panel/observation identities, resolved native spectral extraction, source targets and criteria, a submitted-analysis interface plus independent granular verifier, common exposure policy and cumulative budgets. The existing source-code pin and generated software controls do not constitute these delivery/evaluation manifests.

improvement.rationale: Task identity binds the explicitly released future canonical preimage; atomic binder adoption must produce exactly those bytes. The unchanged improvement contract supplies no justified superiority metric for maximizing descriptive developmental associations. A new held-out predictor would change the task. In addition, the common authentic data, historical estimator, independent verifier, exposure and budget protocols are not frozen. Neither information condition has an admissible improvement protocol; this does not make descriptive reproduction ineligible.
